candidate_rule: two non-promoted evidence candidates per source record: verified fact and explicit scope limitation

documents.title: Mobile Matters: download speeds, connection rates and latency levels revealed

documents.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Building Digital UK
documents.title: Rural Scots get mobile signal boost as 50th UK Government-funded mast goes live

documents.publisher: Building Digital UK and Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
documents.title: Check your gigabit broadband availability
Shared Rural Network Wellbeing Survey Wave 1 Findings report

records.fact: Ofcom found that 71% of measured cellular network connections were on 4G, seven percentage points lower than one year earlier.
records.scope_limit: Crowdsourced connection shares describe observed devices and periods; they do not prove technology availability at an exact address.

records.fact: Twenty-eight per cent of measured connections were on 5G, nine percentage points higher year on year.
records.scope_limit: A national observed share does not establish 5G service, indoor reception or handset compatibility at a parcel.

records.fact: Ofcom reported that 0.7% of measured cellular connections were on 3G.
records.scope_limit: The measured share is not a current operator-by-address coverage result.

records.fact: Ofcom reported that 0.2% of measured cellular connections were on 2G.
records.scope_limit: A small observed share does not prove 2G availability, dependence or retirement timing for an exact premises.

records.fact: In urban UK areas, 29% of measured network connections were on 5G.
records.scope_limit: The urban aggregate does not predict coverage or performance at a particular postcode or building.

records.fact: In rural UK areas, 19% of measured network connections were on 5G.
records.scope_limit: The rural aggregate cannot identify which rural premises have usable 5G.

records.fact: The average time to download a 2 MB file was 0.3 seconds on 5G.
records.scope_limit: An average measured file time is not a guaranteed speed or latency result for an address or device.

records.fact: The average time to download a 2 MB file was 0.7 seconds on 4G.
records.scope_limit: The result is a study average and cannot establish local congestion or indoor performance.

records.fact: The average time to download a 2 MB file was 4.9 seconds on 3G.
records.scope_limit: The result does not guarantee the experience of any specific user, location or application.

records.fact: Two per cent of measured network connections used standalone 5G.
records.scope_limit: The national sample share does not establish standalone 5G availability for a parcel or subscription.

records.fact: Ofcom reported file download times on standalone 5G were about 45% faster on average than on non-standalone 5G.
records.scope_limit: The comparative average does not guarantee an individual speed gain and depends on network, device and conditions.

records.fact: Average connection success was 96% for standalone 5G and 98% for non-standalone 5G.
records.scope_limit: Study-wide success rates cannot determine whether a session will connect at a given location or time.

records.fact: EE had the highest measured proportion of network connections on 5G at 32%.
records.scope_limit: An operator-level national share is not an address-specific coverage or performance ranking.

records.fact: Vodafone had the lowest measured 5G share at 24% and the highest 4G share at 76%.
records.scope_limit: Observed connection mix does not establish local availability or which operator is best for a parcel.

records.fact: O2 had the lowest measured 4G share at 68% and the highest measured 3G share at 3%.
records.scope_limit: National sample shares cannot be converted into exact-address network truth.

records.fact: Fifty UK Government-funded 4G masts had been switched on in rural Scotland by 9 July 2026.
records.scope_limit: A switched-on mast count does not prove signal, capacity or service from every operator at a particular premises.

records.fact: The government-funded upgrades were providing 4G coverage from all four mobile network operators across more than 1,900 square kilometres of rural Scotland.
records.scope_limit: The aggregate area does not establish usable indoor or outdoor service at every point within the footprint.

records.fact: Across Great Britain, UK Government funding had activated more than 140 4G masts through the Shared Rural Network.
records.scope_limit: A national activated-site total is programme evidence, not an address-level coverage result.

records.fact: UK Government investment had connected more than 153,000 homes and businesses in Scotland's hardest-to-reach areas to gigabit-capable broadband.
records.scope_limit: The cumulative count does not identify the UPRNs, current provider or retail orderability of an individual property.

records.fact: The Shared Rural Network reached its target of 4G coverage from at least one operator across 95% of UK landmass a year ahead of schedule.
records.scope_limit: Geographic coverage predictions do not guarantee indoor reception, capacity or service at a specific address.

records.fact: Since 2019, Scotland's 4G geographic coverage from at least one operator increased from 80% to 90%.
records.scope_limit: Nation-level predicted geographic coverage cannot be assigned to a parcel.

records.fact: The programme expected Scotland's 4G geographic coverage from at least one operator to reach 91% by the end of the programme.
records.scope_limit: A future programme expectation is not completed-build or orderability evidence.

records.fact: Scotland's geographic coverage from all mobile network operators increased from 41% to 71%.
records.scope_limit: The national prediction does not prove all-operator availability at an exact point or premises.

records.fact: The 50th funded Scottish mast was activated near Branault on the Ardnamurchan peninsula.
records.scope_limit: A named mast location does not prove the coverage boundary or service status of nearby parcels.

records.fact: The programme reported that the Scottish upgrades were almost all made to existing masts, with new masts used where suitable infrastructure did not exist.
records.scope_limit: The deployment approach does not establish the configuration, operator participation or performance of any individual site.

records.fact: The government gigabit availability checker is provided for addresses in England and Wales, with separate services for Scotland and Northern Ireland.
records.scope_limit: The service's geographic scope does not itself prove broadband availability for an entered address.

records.fact: As of 7 July 2026, checker data came from the January Open Market Review published in June 2026.
records.scope_limit: The source snapshot may lag supplier changes and must not be treated as real-time orderability evidence.

records.fact: The checker stated that its next data update was scheduled for September 2026.
records.scope_limit: A scheduled update does not guarantee that a supplier plan or address status remains unchanged before that date.

records.fact: The checker states that data will be updated every four months after the September 2026 update.
records.scope_limit: A periodic refresh cycle means the displayed status may not reflect the newest provider information.

records.fact: The official disclaimer says supplier plans may change and complete accuracy of an address's gigabit status cannot be guaranteed.
records.scope_limit: Checker output must remain qualified and cannot be promoted as infallible parcel truth.

records.fact: The SRN baseline survey included 1,285 participants: 1,247 residents and 38 businesses.
records.scope_limit: The participant sample is not a census and cannot establish conditions for every rural household or business.

records.fact: Survey fieldwork ran from 15 July to 13 September 2024 across rural communities in all four UK nations.
records.scope_limit: The fieldwork period predates later network changes and does not measure current exact-address service.

records.fact: Ninety-one per cent of participants reported going online at least once a day.
records.scope_limit: Self-reported frequency does not measure connection quality or availability at a parcel.

records.fact: Forty-three per cent of participants said they went online more than ten times a day.
records.scope_limit: Usage frequency is self-reported behaviour and not empirical network-performance evidence.

records.fact: Four per cent reported going online less than once a month or never.
records.scope_limit: The survey result does not identify whether low use was caused by coverage, affordability, preference or another factor.

records.fact: At their address, 53% rated mobile internet value for money as very or fairly good.
records.scope_limit: A perception rating from sampled participants is not an address-specific tariff or service-quality measurement.

records.fact: At their address, 46% rated mobile internet speed as very or fairly good.
records.scope_limit: Self-reported speed perception does not establish measured throughput at any parcel.

records.fact: At their address, 44% rated mobile internet reliability as very or fairly good.
records.scope_limit: The sample perception cannot determine reliability for another address, operator or time period.

records.fact: At their address, 40% rated mobile internet coverage and availability as very or fairly good.
records.scope_limit: A survey rating is not an engineering coverage prediction or live provider check.

records.fact: When out and about, 56% rated mobile internet coverage and availability as very or fairly good.
records.scope_limit: The aggregate perception cannot predict coverage at a specific journey, road segment or premises.
